name: Gao Nang Thom Cho Dao
summary: A long-grain, one-crop rice from Mỹ Lệ in Chợ Đào, pink inside the grain and fragrant as soon as the pot boils, cooked glossy and sticky. The variety has faded since a dike ended the yearly flood, and the commune is restoring it.
origin: Xã Mỹ Lệ, Chợ Đào, in the old Cần Đước land of the old Long An half.
texture: The grain is long, pomegranate-pink when broken open, and glossy once cooked, as if tossed with oil.
taste: Fragrant as soon as the pot boils, then sticky and still fragrant the next day.
The variety lost much of that character after a closed dike ended the yearly flood, salt, and silt, and chemical fertilizer tired the soil. The commune has marked 200 ha to restore it.
howToEat: Cook it as rice, or carry a bag home. People still ask for it at Tết.
It is a one-crop rice of 170 to 185 days, sown in lunar June or July and cut in lunar December.
seoDescription: Nàng Thơm Chợ Đào, a one-crop rice from Mỹ Lệ, fragrant when the pot boils.
